subject: What changes between bedtime and 2am?
preheader: Frame the overnight equipment question before arranging a complex paediatric trial.
intro: For a child or young person with complex physical support needs, what looks workable at 2pm may not answer the questions that emerge at 2am.
The purpose of a home trial is not to promise an outcome. It is to help the clinical and family discussion draw on observations from ordinary use.
body: The relevant question may involve positioning, transfers, care routines, access, configuration or how the equipment works within the home environment.
Being clear about that question helps everyone understand what should be observed and what the trial can realistically contribute.
questions: Which overnight routine or task needs to be understood?
Who needs to use or support the equipment at home?
Which configuration variables need to be tested?
What observations would be useful to the clinical decision?
actionTitle: Talk through the trial before choosing the product
actionText: Sleep Choice can help OTs work through a bed or mattress trial pathway for a complex brief. Reply with a de-identified equipment question and we will help determine whether an in-home trial is practical and what needs to be configured.
boundary: A home trial supports the equipment discussion. It does not replace clinical assessment, family and care-team input, safeguarding requirements or individual clinical judgement.
trialFooterText: Seven-night in-home trial availability, service area, equipment configuration and individual arrangements are confirmed per case.
